title: Capacity Sprint Switchover: Tactical Staff Pools, Rolling Decommit, and Impacted-Feature Scoring
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a lightweight operational protocol for mid-cycle capacity shocks: how to shift tactical staff pools, execute rolling decommits against lower-priority features, score feature-eviction impact, and communicate decisions to stakeholders.
goal: Reduce mid-cycle decision lead time to <= 24 hours for staff reassignments
Establish a repeatable scoring rubric for scope eviction that preserves high-customer-value work
Create a comms and rollback checklist to avoid accidental de-scoping of compliance or Dedicated/Private work
acceptance_criteria: Scoring rubric published in Confluence and reviewed by Eng/Design/SRE
Runbook created with step-by-step reassignment flows and Slack/on-call notification templates
Two simulated dry-run drills completed with stakeholders and retrospective notes captured
Automated dashboard widget created to show post-trim velocity and active critical-path owners
decisions: Adopt a 3-tier scope eviction score (customer-value, cross-team dependency, compliance risk) with weighted sum approach
Reserve a 10% tactical staff pool across Backend/Platform/Console as the default surge channel for first two weeks of any cycle
Require SRE sign-off before any decommit affecting Dedicated or Private deployment capabilities

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-eager decommits may cascade into infra changes — Mitigation: SRE gating and 'no decommit' flag for Dedicated/Private features
Risk: Staff pool starvation for ongoing incident response — Mitigation: maintain a 1-FTE on-call buffer and use burst credits rather than permanent reassignments
Risk: Customer surprise from scope eviction — Mitigation: pre-defined customer communication templates and Sales/CS alignment step in playbook
